When you open Able, at most once every 24 hours. It only checks: nothing is downloaded until you tap Download and install.

Android lets an app install APK files only after you allow it in “Install unknown apps”. Turn on “Allow from this source” for Able, then come back and tap Download and install again. You can turn it off again at any time; Android always asks you to confirm every installation.

Android refused the update: its signature differs from the installed Able (or it is an older build). An update installs only if it is signed with the same key. To switch to this APK, export a backup, uninstall Able and install the APK from GitHub.
Android or a device policy blocked the installation.
Android reports that the APK is invalid or damaged. Nothing was installed.
Not enough storage to install the update.
Android could not install the update.

Able contacts only GitHub. A check reads the public release list of github.com/dragolab/able from raw.githubusercontent.com (or api.github.com). Only when you tap Download and install, Able downloads the release APK from github.com, which redirects to GitHub\'s download server (githubusercontent.com). The requests carry only what any connection needs (your IP address and the generic name “Able-Updater”): no account, device identifier, settings, apps or usage data are sent, and GitHub\'s privacy policy applies to them. The APK is saved in Able\'s cache, checked against the size GitHub publishes and installed only after you confirm in Android\'s dialog; Android accepts it only if it is signed with the same key as the installed Able. The automatic check runs at most once every 24 hours when you open Able, never downloads anything and can be turned off here.
